key_insight: ArogyaSutra combines multimodal inputs, tool grounding, and multi-agent reasoning to improve medical question answering in English and seven Indic languages.
clinical_relevance: The framework could make AI-assisted healthcare more accessible in multilingual, low-resource settings where patients communicate using local languages and medical images.
method: Built ArogyaBodha, a multilingual multimodal medical QA dataset from 8 heterogeneous sources.
Covers 31 body systems, 6 imaging modalities, and 21 clinical domains across 8 languages.
Uses an actor-critic multi-agent design with dual-memory and trajectory distillation for step-wise reasoning.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports improved multilingual medical reasoning accuracy across all Indic languages, with ablations supporting each major component.
watch_item: Performance gains from benchmark experiments may not fully translate to real-world clinical workflows without careful validation, language coverage checks, and safety review.
paper_title: ArogyaSutra: A Multi-Agent Framework for Multimodal Medical Reasoning in Indic Languages
